item.title: ‘Serious error of judgment’: outrage over military AI event at Berlin arts complex
item.description: Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness. A recent event at one of the city’s most legendary clubland institutions, however, has proven too dystopian even for seasoned techno-heads. On 11 November, the Kraftwerk Berlin arts complex had its central hall transformed into what visitors described as something resembling a war room, with maps and aerial footage projected on to concrete walls, drones hanging from the ceiling, and guards in flak jackets patrolling the premises with sniffer dogs. Continue reading...

item.title: Labour MPs sign up for leadership course to counter rightwing populism
item.description: Course run by former No 10 advisers is funded by Gary Lubner, who has given more than £11m to Labour More than 20 Labour MPs have signed up to a year-long leadership course helping them to counter rightwing populism and deal with hostility, run by two former No 10 advisers and ultimately funded by multimillionaire donor Gary Lubner. The training courses worth about £9,600 are being led by Ruth Turner, who was Tony Blair’s director of government relations, and Peter Hyman, who has worked for Blair, Keir Starmer and Andy Burnham’s governments. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations
item.description: The effects of the continent’s coming polls will be felt far and wide – and could well turn into ‘key tests’ of the bloc’s resilience In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them. Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it. Continue reading...

item.description: COP31 climate talks in Turkey have gone into overtime, with deep divisions over fossil fuels, climate finance and global warming targets delaying an agreement. A revised draft dropped all mention of fossil fuels, prompting strong criticism from the EU and a dozen countries demanding a clear commitment to phase them out. Negotiators are also split over a proposed global electrification target, carbon capture and the future of UN climate science reports. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations. In their nine votes to six majority ruling, the panel of judges in The Hague set out a detailed roadmap for how the convention should be applied to real-world situations in which a government is accused of committing genocide against a whole population group, especially when it comes to assessing the question of intent. For almost a decade, the Rohingya have awaited this moment; recognition from the international court of justice (ICJ) that Myanmar in 2017 intentionally tried to destroy the mostly Muslim minority group through a campaign of mass killings and rape. item.title: Are Nigerian Artists Dominating the Grammys’ Best African Music Performance Category?
